crosswalk_hints.notes: Strong conceptual match to CHR Adult Smoking and AHR Smoking; align year, age adjustment, modeling, and geography.
Only compare after enforcing age 18-64 and reconciling survey question/source with ACS/SAHIE.
Same no-leisure-activity concept feeds multiple health rankings, but county products may model several years.
AHR may publish the positive inverse (high health status); do not compare signs without normalization.

research_notes: The Delaware report is a public table-level codebook and CDC supplies a complete public-use variable codebook. The catalog's measure phrases are not column names; use CDC raw/calculated names. Question wording, availability, and derived-variable versions change by year.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Strong definitional match with BRFSS/CHR; reconcile period and adjustment.
Household survey prevalence; not directly comparable to Feeding America person-level modeled estimates.
Match linked/period method and pooled years with Delaware Vital/HRSA/March of Dimes.
Crosswalk to ACS/CHR/NLIHC only after selecting burden threshold versus composite.
Compare individual provider classes, never the combined label.

research_notes: AHR has a published measure dictionary and a typed GraphQL schema. The catalog lists a very broad set spanning multiple AHR report series; always preserve report edition, measureId, population/subpopulation, date interval, unit, and source. API use requires registration/key and is limited by publisher terms.

sources.source_name: Delaware Annual Economic Report (Delaware Department of Labor)
sources.summary: 9 public documentation artifacts located; coverage is partial and remaining intake labels are inferred.

codebook_artifacts.title: Delaware Annual Economic Report 2024
codebook_artifacts.authority: Delaware Department of Labor, Office of Occupational and Labor Market Information
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Delaware population, labor force, employment, wages, GDP, industries, counties/cities, and projections
codebook_artifacts.notes: Tables provide published labels, units, periods, sources, and `*` disclosure notation, but no standalone report data dictionary was found.

codebook_artifacts.title: Delaware LMI Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Employment and wages by industry and area
codebook_artifacts.notes: Underlying administrative program for many report employment/wage tables.

codebook_artifacts.title: BLS QCEW Overview
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: QCEW coverage, concepts, and production
codebook_artifacts.notes: QCEW covers about 95% of U.S. jobs via unemployment-insurance records; counts jobs by place of work.

codebook_artifacts.title: BLS QCEW Data Overview
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: QCEW files, fields, geography, industry, disclosure, and revisions
codebook_artifacts.notes: Use for machine-readable extracts underlying report tables.

codebook_artifacts.title: BLS QCEW Questions and Answers
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Employment, wage, coverage, confidentiality, and comparison definitions
codebook_artifacts.notes: Clarifies filled-job counting, multiple-job holders, exclusions, and wage contents.

codebook_artifacts.title: Delaware LMI Local Area Unemployment Statistics
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Resident labor force, employment, unemployment, and unemployment rate
codebook_artifacts.notes: Household/residence-based labor-market series.

codebook_artifacts.title: BLS LAUS Frequently Asked Questions
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: LAUS concepts, model-based estimation, geography, revisions, and comparability
codebook_artifacts.notes: Explains why LAUS resident employment differs from establishment/QCEW job counts.

codebook_artifacts.title: BEA GDP by State Methodology
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: State GDP and industry contributions
codebook_artifacts.notes: Underlying definitions and methods for report GDP content.

codebook_artifacts.title: Census Population Estimates Technical Documentation
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Population and migration estimates
codebook_artifacts.notes: Population vintages can revise historical estimates.

variables.label: Additional dollars needed to be food secure

variables.label: NIBRS crime incident
variables.definition: One or more offenses committed by the same offender or group of offenders acting together at the same time and place.
categories: May contain one or multiple offenses
comparability_notes: Do not substitute offense counts for incident counts. This distinction is also crucial when comparing to DVCC, whose table unit is a domestic-violence incident.

variables.label: Offenses cleared
variables.definition: An offense is cleared when a suspect is arrested and referred for prosecution, or exceptionally cleared when the offender is clearly identifiable but cannot be arrested under qualifying circumstances; percent cleared is the cleared share reported for an offense grouping.
variables.universe: Reported offenses eligible for the report's clearance calculation
comparability_notes: A clearance is not a conviction. Timing can cross calendar years, so a simple same-year cleared-count/offense-count interpretation may be misleading without the report methodology.

variables.label: Reported offense rate
variables.definition: Number of offenses divided by the relevant population and multiplied by 1,000.
variables.universe: Reported offenses and resident population for the stated geography/year
comparability_notes: Population estimates can revise; preserve the denominator vintage. Not directly comparable to STIPDA rates, which are typically injuries/deaths per 100,000 residents.

variables.label: Reported/known offenses received by law enforcement
variables.definition: Crimes reported to or otherwise known by law enforcement; each charge within an incident is counted as an offense received.
variables.universe: NIBRS-reportable offenses known to participating Delaware law-enforcement agencies
variables.geography: Delaware; county, agency and municipality where tabulated
categories: Group B arrest-only offense where applicable
missing_codes: Incomplete agency submissions can produce undercounts
suppression_rules: No general cell-suppression rule is stated; small counts are published in many tables.
comparability_notes: This is not a unique-incident or unique-victim count. Multiple charges in one incident are counted separately, and only crime known to police is included.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Crime data count police-known offenses/charges; MCDRC counts reviewed deaths; STIPDA counts resident deaths or hospital discharges. Harmonize intent, fatality status, age, residency and year before comparison.
DVCC incidents are flagged by relationship/context and may be criminal or non-criminal; Crime in Delaware is offense-centered NIBRS reporting. Never assume one DV incident equals one offense.

research_notes: The report itself supplies a substantial public glossary and FBI-derived offense definitions. Known limitations include crime not reported to police, the 2020-2021 pandemic disruption, changes in classification practices, and incomplete 2024 homicide submissions described in the edition.

variables.label: Crude or age-adjusted injury death rate
variables.definition: Injury deaths divided by population and expressed per 100,000; age-adjusted rates standardize the age distribution as documented in the product.
variables.universe: Delaware-resident injury deaths and corresponding population denominator
suppression_rules: Follow workbook footnotes for small/unstable rates.
comparability_notes: Crude and age-adjusted rates are not interchangeable. Crime in Delaware uses per-1,000 offense rates, so units and numerators differ.

variables.label: Intent classification
variables.definition: Whether the injury was unintentional, self-inflicted, assault/homicide, undetermined, or another intent category used by STIPDA.
variables.universe: Qualifying injury deaths/discharges with usable intent coding
comparability_notes: Fatal and nonfatal labels differ (suicide versus self-harm attempt; homicide versus assault). Do not collapse without retaining outcome type.

variables.label: Mechanism/cause of injury
variables.definition: External mechanism category used to organize injury events, including falls, drowning, fire/burn, firearm, motor-vehicle traffic, poisoning and other mechanisms.
variables.universe: Qualifying injury events with usable mechanism coding
comparability_notes: Mechanism and intent are orthogonal: firearm is a mechanism and may be suicide, homicide, unintentional or undetermined. Preserve both dimensions.

variables.label: Resident injury deaths
variables.definition: Deaths of Delaware residents classified within the STIPDA injury case definition, tabulated by intent/mechanism and demographic group.
variables.universe: Delaware-resident deaths meeting the injury case definition
variables.time_granularity: five-year pooled period and component year where workbook provides it
missing_codes: Unknown/unspecified intent or mechanism where reported
suppression_rules: Workbook-specific small-number/reliability conventions must be read from the relevant sheet; no unified public field dictionary was located.
comparability_notes: Death-certificate injury mortality is not police offense data or hospital discharge data. Restrict comparisons to the same resident universe and ICD/case-definition era.

variables.label: Resident inpatient injury discharges
variables.definition: Hospital discharges for Delaware residents admitted to Delaware inpatient facilities and meeting the injury case definition; out-of-state hospital care, clinic/surgicenter care and emergency-department-only visits are excluded.
variables.universe: Delaware residents discharged from Delaware inpatient facilities with qualifying injury diagnosis
missing_codes: Missing/invalid external-cause coding can exclude mechanism/intent classification
suppression_rules: Follow workbook footnotes for small/unstable cells.
comparability_notes: A discharge is not a unique person; readmissions can be counted. Coverage excludes Delaware residents treated outside the state.

crosswalk_hints.notes: STIPDA uses health outcomes, Crime in Delaware uses offenses/charges, and DVCC uses police incidents. Align fatal/nonfatal status, external cause, relationship, unit and denominator.
STIPDA is vital-statistics population surveillance; MCDRC is case review. MCDRC may add circumstances but review-year totals are not incidence counts.

research_notes: Published methodology and table workbooks exist, but no consolidated row-level dictionary was located. The web index is historical: mortality extends later than hospitalization on the page, so comparisons should not assume common years.

codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Age-cohort projection tables
codebook_artifacts.notes: Provides annual projections at finer age resolution than the report summary.

codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Detailed age-by-race/ethnicity-by-sex projection tables
codebook_artifacts.notes: Race groups are mutually exclusive as documented; age runs through 100-plus.

variables.label: Estimated peak-season population associated with seasonal housing
variables.definition: Seasonal population estimate for June through August derived from seasonal/vacant housing assumptions, including an 80 percent occupancy assumption and 2.64 persons per occupied seasonal unit in the 2024.0 report; it excludes hotels, motels, campgrounds, recreational vehicles and day visitors.
variables.universe: Persons associated with occupied seasonal housing under DPC assumptions
comparability_notes: Not a year-round resident population and excludes several visitor-accommodation types. Use the PDF's version-specific 2.64-person assumption; do not substitute conflicting summary-page text.

variables.label: Five-year population-change components
variables.definition: Projected births and deaths over a five-year interval and net migration defined as in-migrants minus out-migrants; report tables mark five-year totals beginning with the specified year.
variables.universe: Population component events for the projection geography
variables.geography: Delaware and counties/major cities where table provides
comparability_notes: These are interval totals, unlike July 1 population point estimates. Net migration can be negative and is not gross in- or out-migration.

variables.label: Mutually exclusive projection race/ethnicity
variables.definition: Projection classification consisting of White alone non-Hispanic, Black alone non-Hispanic, Hispanic of any race, and Other non-Hispanic; Other includes principally Asian and multiracial populations, and multiple-race records are assigned to Other non-Hispanic.
comparability_notes: Not directly comparable with ACS tables that publish Asian, AI/AN, NHPI, some-other-race and two-or-more-races separately, nor with school-survey mark-all-that-apply race questions.

variables.source_variable_name: Jobs by place of work / jobs by residence / net commuting
variables.label: Projected employment and commuting balance
variables.definition: Place-of-work jobs are jobs located in the geography and exclude self-employed, private-household and direct-farm employment under the report definition. Jobs by residence represent employed residents and can reflect multiple jobs; net commuting is inflow minus outflow.
variables.universe: Covered employment and employed residents in projection geographies
comparability_notes: Jobs are not unique workers; a person may hold multiple jobs. Preserve exclusions and the sign convention for net commuting.

variables.label: Projected occupied households
variables.definition: Projected household count for the stated geography and July 1 year using the DPC household projection method.
comparability_notes: A household is not a housing unit; vacant units are excluded. Household change tables may be interval changes rather than point estimates.

variables.label: Projected resident population as of July 1
variables.definition: Cohort-component projection beginning with the July 1, 2020 population by age, race/ethnicity and sex and applying survival, fertility and migration assumptions.
variables.universe: Resident population in the projection geography
variables.geography: Delaware, counties, Wilmington, Dover and Newark; separate municipal products where published
suppression_rules: No general small-cell suppression stated for public projection tables.
comparability_notes: A projection is not an ACS estimate or actual enrollment count. Retain projection version because assumptions and historical controls can change.

crosswalk_hints.notes: DPC projections may be used for planning scenarios, but published rate series often use Census estimates. A comparison function should never silently replace the publisher's denominator.

source_variable_names: DDOE/KIDS COUNT/PRAMS/YRBS race and ethnicity variables
crosswalk_hints.notes: DPC's four mutually exclusive groups collapse Asian and multiracial into Other non-Hispanic. Harmonization requires an explicit loss-of-detail flag.

research_notes: The PDF and workbooks form a public codebook/methodology package. Table footnotes distinguish July 1 point estimates from five-year totals. Version 2024.0 is the currently adopted series documented at research time, even though the 2025 meeting adopted it without a new projection vintage.

variables.definition: Items include ever experiencing the specified negative feelings, frequency of getting help, self-rated emotional health from excellent to very bad, and 0-10 ladder ratings for current life and expected life in five years.
variables.time_granularity: item-specific; current and expected five-year life evaluation
categories: 0 worst possible life through 10 best possible life
comparability_notes: Self-rated emotional health, negative affect and life satisfaction are distinct. They are not diagnoses and should not be merged with PRAMS depression-diagnosis variables or YRBS sadness/suicidality without exact wording review.

variables.label: Nonschool screen, gaming, physical activity and reading time
variables.definition: Separate items ask usual nonschool online/TV time, video-game time, physically active play/exercise/sports time and reading-for-pleasure time.
comparability_notes: Do not sum online/TV and video games without checking overlap. Physical-activity wording and duration differ from YRBS days-with-60-minutes indicators.

variables.label: Race or ethnicity, mark all that apply
variables.definition: Student-selected race/ethnicity categories on the 2025 grade-5 instrument, with multiple responses permitted.
variables.geography: Delaware public schools; reportable state/local breakouts
categories: Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander
suppression_rules: Public table suppression/reliability rules are report-specific; no complete public microdata rulebook was located.
comparability_notes: Not mutually exclusive. Do not directly compare with DPC's mutually exclusive four-group race/ethnicity projection without a documented derivation.

variables.label: Recency/frequency of eight substance behaviors
variables.definition: Frequency items cover cigarettes, vaping, cigars, chewing tobacco, alcohol, marijuana, dactyls and prescription-drug misuse using a common ordered response set.
categories: Used before but not in past year
A few times in past year
comparability_notes: These categories are not equivalent to YRBS past-30-day day counts. Any binary current-use crosswalk is inferred and must state its chosen threshold.

variables.label: School bullying, electronic bullying and witnessed violence at home
variables.definition: Q35 asks whether the student was bullied at school in the past 30 days; Q37 asks about electronic bullying in the past 30 days; Q38 asks whether the student has witnessed adults at home hurting one another.
variables.time_granularity: past 30 days for bullying; lifetime/unspecified ever wording for witnessed home violence as printed
comparability_notes: Keep school bullying, electronic bullying and home violence separate. Q38 is a student's self-report and is not equivalent to DVCC's police-recorded 'children present' flag.

School/electronic bullying, witnessed household violence and police-recorded child presence are related but non-equivalent constructs.

source_variable_names: YRBS sadness, mental-health and suicidality items

research_notes: Public questionnaires and domain/trend documents support a partial codebook, but no public record-layout dictionary or downloadable microdata file was located; access is by data request. DSS is annual and principally covers grades 5, 8 and 11, whereas YRBS is biennial and targets different middle/high-school grade universes. COVID-era missing 2020 administration and 2021 mode/participation changes should be flagged in trends.

variables.label: Exposure to secondhand smoke
variables.definition: Questionnaire measures assessing exposure to smoke produced by other people's tobacco use.
comparability_notes: Keep home, vehicle, school and public-place exposure items separate if the questionnaire distinguishes them.

variables.label: Exposure to tobacco marketing
variables.definition: Questionnaire measures of exposure to or recognition of tobacco-industry marketing.
comparability_notes: Marketing channel and product categories can change materially across survey years, especially with electronic cigarettes.

variables.label: Participation in tobacco-prevention programs
variables.definition: Questionnaire measures indicating whether a student participated in tobacco prevention programming.
comparability_notes: Participation is an exposure to programming, not evidence of program effectiveness; compare only after matching program definition and recall period.

variables.label: Student grade
variables.definition: Grade of the participating student; the published universe spans grades 6 through 12.
variables.universe: Random sample of students in grades 6-12 in Delaware school districts
variables.geography: Delaware; district/school estimates may be restricted
suppression_rules: No Delaware public-use suppression rule was located; school/district microdata availability is not documented on the YTS archive page.
comparability_notes: Do not equate with CDC NYTS middle-school/high-school grouping without recoding grades consistently.

variables.label: Tobacco-use behavior
variables.definition: Questionnaire measures of student behaviors associated with tobacco use. Exact product, ever-use, current-use and frequency fields must be read from the applicable Delaware questionnaire.
variables.time_granularity: survey administration; recall period is item-specific
comparability_notes: A national convention often defines current use as use on at least 1 of the past 30 days, but that definition is not assigned to a Delaware field until verified in the year-specific Delaware instrument.

variables.label: youth tobacco use
comparability_notes: The phrase was imported from the SHIP resource guide and has not been verified as a field name or publisher-defined measure.
variables.inference_basis: The SHIP intake workbook lists this phrase in a measures cell. No exact publisher-documented variable matched during this research pass.

variables.label: YTS administration year
variables.definition: Even-numbered year in which the Delaware school-based survey was administered.
comparability_notes: Survey availability and instrument content vary by year; 2020 and other pandemic-era collection conditions should be checked in the year-specific instrument/report.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Crosswalk to NYTS only after matching product, recall window, threshold (ever/current/frequent), grade universe, weighting and survey year.
Program participation is not comparable to service utilization counts unless both count the same student-level exposure and period.

research_notes: Delaware questionnaires are publicly indexed, but a Delaware consolidated codebook with stable variable names, value labels, weights, design variables and missing-value codes was not found. The exact Delaware field mapping must therefore be extracted questionnaire-by-questionnaire or requested with the microdata. National NYTS documentation is authoritative for NYTS, but is only a comparison aid and was not used to invent Delaware field names.

variables.label: Adequate provider data indicator
variables.definition: Indicates whether sufficiently complete provider-reported vaccination data were obtained for the child.
comparability_notes: Provider-based coverage variables generally require PDAT; denominator differs from all household-interview respondents.

variables.label: Age group
variables.definition: Age group of the sampled young child at interview.
comparability_notes: Coverage assessed by a milestone age (for example by 24 or 36 months) is distinct from age at interview.

variables.label: At least 1 measles-containing dose by 36 months
variables.definition: Indicator that provider records show one or more qualifying measles-containing vaccine doses by 36 months.
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation area
comparability_notes: Measles-containing vaccine may be MMR or another qualifying formulation; use CDC definition.

variables.label: At least 2 influenza doses by 24 months with minimum spacing
variables.definition: Indicator for two or more influenza vaccine doses by 24 months, with doses separated by at least the codebook-defined interval (four weeks less four days).
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation area
comparability_notes: Spacing rule is part of the definition; do not compare with any-two-flu-doses counts that ignore interval.

variables.label: At least 3 hepatitis B doses by 36 months
variables.definition: Indicator that provider records show at least three qualifying hepatitis B vaccine doses by 36 months.
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation area
comparability_notes: Do not confuse with P_UTDHEPA1/P_UTDHEPA2, which refer to hepatitis A.

variables.label: At least 3 poliovirus doses by 36 months
variables.definition: Indicator that provider records show at least three qualifying poliovirus vaccine doses by 36 months.
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation area
comparability_notes: Match dose threshold and cutoff age before comparing to registry or claims measures.

variables.label: At least 4 DT-containing doses by 36 months
variables.definition: Indicator that provider records show four or more qualifying DT-containing doses by 36 months.
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation area
suppression_rules: Estimate suppression/reliability flags are applied in publication products, not encoded by this binary alone.
comparability_notes: Match antigen, required dose count and age cutoff exactly; not a general 'fully vaccinated' measure.

variables.label: Combined 4:3:1:3:3:1:4 vaccine series
variables.definition: Indicator that the child is up to date for the specified combined vaccine series: 4 DTaP, 3 polio, 1 measles-containing, 3 Hib, 3 hepatitis B, 1 varicella and 4 pneumococcal conjugate doses under CDC rules.
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation area
comparability_notes: The compact series name encodes dose counts; compare only to a combined-series measure with the identical antigens, counts and age cutoff.

variables.label: Final provider-phase sampling weight
variables.definition: Final weight for analyses of children with adequate provider data; the continental-U.S./state analytic weight excludes territories as documented.
variables.geography: United States/states under the documented weight scope
comparability_notes: Use with design variables and the correct domain; not interchangeable with household-interview weights.

variables.label: Hepatitis A dose-series indicators
variables.definition: Provider-based indicators for at least one and at least two qualifying hepatitis A doses by the codebook-defined age cutoff.
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation area
comparability_notes: Keep the one-dose and two-dose thresholds separate; neither is interchangeable with hepatitis B field P_UTDHEP.

variables.label: Income-to-poverty category
variables.definition: Household income relative to poverty, categorized for vaccination-coverage analysis.
comparability_notes: Can be conceptually aligned to NSCH FPL implicates only after matching thresholds; NIS field is categorical and not the same imputation structure.

variables.label: Number of diphtheria/tetanus/pertussis-containing doses by 36 months
variables.definition: Provider-reported count of qualifying DT-containing vaccine doses received by 36 months of age.
variables.geography: United States, state and estimation-area analyses
missing_codes: . = no adequate provider data, as documented
suppression_rules: Published estimates are subject to CDC reliability criteria; consult report footnotes.
comparability_notes: Dose count differs from series-up-to-date indicator P_UTDTP4 and from doses recorded only in a state registry.

variables.label: Race/ethnicity of child
variables.definition: Public-use combined race and Hispanic ethnicity classification for the child.
categories: Use exact 2024 codebook labels; public-use categories combine race and Hispanic origin
suppression_rules: Public-use category detail is constrained by disclosure/reliability considerations.
comparability_notes: Do not merge with HUD's 2025 race/ethnicity categories without an explicit many-to-one crosswalk; category standards differ.

variables.label: Sampling stratum
variables.definition: Public-use stratum variable for variance estimation under the NIS complex sample design.
suppression_rules: Public-use design coding may combine or mask operational strata.
comparability_notes: Use only with documented survey-design procedures, not as a substantive geography.

variables.label: True state of residence FIPS code
variables.definition: State-of-residence code used for state estimates.
suppression_rules: Finer location is not implied by this state field.
comparability_notes: Crosswalk directly to NSCH FIPSST after aligning year and population universe.

variables.label: Unique child identifier
variables.definition: Public-use sequence number uniquely identifying the sampled child record.
suppression_rules: Identifier is survey-specific and not linkable to external identity.
comparability_notes: Do not treat as a stable longitudinal person identifier.

comparability_notes: The phrase was imported from the SHIP resource guide and has not been verified as a field name or publisher-defined measure.
variables.inference_basis: The SHIP intake workbook lists this phrase in a measures cell. No exact publisher-documented variable matched during this research pass.

variables.label: WIC participation history/current participation
variables.definition: Household interview indicators for whether the child ever received WIC and whether the child currently receives WIC, as separately coded.
variables.universe: NIS-Child interviewed children subject to questionnaire routing
comparability_notes: WIC receipt is an assistance-program indicator, not vaccination coverage or a count of WIC service encounters.

crosswalk_hints.notes: STATE can align to NSCH FIPSST; age must remain 19-35-month bands rather than generic child age.
Normalize as weighted share of eligible children only after preserving each antigen, dose threshold, milestone age, provider-data restriction and spacing rule.
Can contextualize WIC/DHSS sources, but the NIS fields are survey responses and do not measure administrative WIC caseload or outcomes.

research_notes: The public-use codebook is complete and supports exact field-level analysis. ChildVaxView may combine multiple estimate products; the NIS-Child public-use file applies to children 19-35 months, while an interactive title may refer more broadly to young children. Use provider-phase weights/design variables and published reliability flags. Provider-reported dose histories, milestone-age logic and combined-series definitions are central comparability constraints.

research_notes: A complete seven-field public dictionary exists for the statewide monthly Medicaid Enrollment dataset. variables.universe: Delaware 211 requests classified to healthcare/COVID assistance

variables.label: Proposed de-identified 211 referral-event dimensions
variables.definition: Comparison-ready fields for contact period, channel, coded need, resource/referral and coarse caller geography, subject to Delaware 211 confirmation.
categories: Channel examples documented publicly: call, text, chat
Need categories must use supplied 211 taxonomy
suppression_rules: Remove direct identifiers and free text; aggregate/suppress sparse geography-category-period cells under Delaware 211 policy.
comparability_notes: Specify whether one row is a contact, need, referral or outcome; one contact can produce multiple need/referral rows.
variables.inference_basis: The official site documents channels, need categories and referrals but publishes no event-level field dictionary.

variables.label: Referral disposition/outcome
variables.definition: Proposed status indicating whether a referral was offered, accepted, contacted or resulted in service, only if Delaware 211 actually collects a standardized follow-up field.
categories: To be supplied by Delaware 211; do not assume fulfilled service
suppression_rules: Aggregate and disclose only standardized codes; exclude case notes/free text.
comparability_notes: A referral does not prove service receipt; absence of outcome may mean no follow-up rather than failed access.
variables.inference_basis: Referral is central to the service, but the public site does not establish that standardized outcome data are collected.

variables.label: Total requests for assistance
variables.definition: Public snapshot count of assistance requests received over the prior 12 months (displayed as 58,000+ at research date).
variables.universe: Requests handled by Delaware 211 during the displayed rolling period
suppression_rules: Displayed with plus sign/rounded threshold; exact count not public on the page.
comparability_notes: A request is a need/contact event, not a unique caller, person, household, referral, fulfilled service or prevalence estimate.

variables.label: Utility-related requests
variables.definition: Requests for utility-related assistance (13,903 in the displayed prior-12-month snapshot).
variables.universe: Delaware 211 requests classified to utility assistance
comparability_notes: Need requests, not approved benefits, households or arrears dollars.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Use as help-seeking event counts, never as prevalence. Normalize by period and population only with caution because awareness/access affect volume.
HUD counts persons/households on one night; Food Bank counts services/outputs; SNAP counts participants/cases. Preserve event/unit distinctions.

research_notes: Delaware 211 publishes selected rolling-12-month aggregates and links to a real-time 211 Counts dashboard, but no export schema/codebook, taxonomy version, deduplication rule, update cadence or suppression policy was located. Detailed community-need/referral data remain request-only. Free text and contact information should never enter a public comparison dataset.

library_id / reporting_period / metric_name / metric_value / metric_unit / age_audience / program_type

Attendance is likely event instances, unlike unique survey respondents or assistance-program participants; request unique-attendee rules before comparison.

research_notes: Historical public schemas and profiles exist, but the catalog's current detailed books/circulation/program-attendance source remains request-only. The Dewey dataset is stale (FY2014-2017) and service_type controls the numeric unit. Profiles explicitly mix current/prior-year values when fields were unreported. A new delivery should include library identifiers, metric units, physical/electronic distinction, program audience/type, uniqueness/deduplication, estimate/substitution flags and reporting-calendar definitions.

variables.definition: Requested event-level or aggregate dimensions for violation timing, exact Title 21 statute, offense description, enforcing unit, coarse location and case/citation disposition.
variables.geography: Troop/coarse location; no exact personal address
categories: Exact statute/offense and disposition code lists must be supplied by DSP
suppression_rules: Remove names, license/vehicle identifiers, exact addresses and narrative; aggregate/suppress sparse cells under DSP policy and law.
comparability_notes: One stop/event can produce multiple charges; define whether one row is stop, citation, charge, arrest or person. Disposition may be held outside DSP.
variables.inference_basis: The annual report proves statute and troop dimensions exist in aggregates, but no public violation-record schema or codebook was found.

variables.source_variable_name: Primary Seatbelt Arrests / Seat Belt Assessments
variables.label: Seat-belt enforcement
variables.definition: Separate counts for primary seat-belt arrests and secondary-violation seat-belt assessments as labeled in the troop tables.
comparability_notes: Primary arrests and secondary assessments are legally/operationally different; keep separate.

variables.source_variable_name: Speed Arrests / 55 MPH Speed Arrests / 65 MPH Speed Arrests
variables.label: Speed-enforcement arrests
variables.definition: Total speeding arrests and subsets reported for 55-mph and 65-mph zones, including troop breakdown tables.
comparability_notes: 55/65-mph counts are subsets of Speed Arrests; do not add them to total speed arrests. Other speed-limit zones remain in total.

variables.label: Total traffic arrests
variables.definition: Total DSP traffic enforcement arrests/citations reported for the calendar year (123,243 in 2025).
variables.universe: Delaware State Police traffic enforcement, DSP only
suppression_rules: Aggregate publication; no suppression rule stated.
comparability_notes: The report uses 'arrests' for enforcement counts/citations; not unique drivers and not criminal arrests in general.

variables.inference_basis: The SHIP intake workbook lists this phrase in a measures cell. No exact publisher-documented variable matched during this research pass.

research_notes: DSP publishes extensive annual aggregate tables but no citation/charge-level public dictionary. The catalog source remains request-only. Key published composites overlap: dangerous moving violations include speed and DUI, and aggressive driving is defined by a statute list. A detailed delivery must state the row unit, multiple-charge handling, statute version, officer/troop versus event geography, void/dismissed/pending treatment, uniqueness rules and disclosure controls.
